excerpt: This risk domain focuses on risks of models with high manipulative capabilities potentially being misused in ways that could reasonably result in large scale harm.
paraphrase: The harmful manipulation risk domain concerns highly manipulative models being misused to cause large-scale harm.

excerpt: Note: The research into harmful manipulation from a severe risk perspective is nascent. The CCL and our assessment of the risk in this domain is exploratory and subject to further research, and may be substantially changed over time.
paraphrase: The note states that research on severe harmful manipulation risk is still early, and this CCL and its risk assessment are exploratory and may change significantly.

section_heading: Table 2.2.3.a: Harmful Manipulation CCLs and Security Mitigations
locator: Table 2.2.3.a / Harmful manipulation level / Recommended security level and rationale
context_stem: Row: Harmful manipulation level; Column: Recommended security level and rationale
excerpt: Security level 2
paraphrase: The recommended security level for the harmful manipulation level CCL is Security level 2.

excerpt: Here, and in other misuse CCLs, we intend this to mean relative to a baseline without generative AI.
paraphrase: Footnote 10 clarifies that comparisons in misuse CCLs are relative to a baseline without generative AI.

excerpt: Mitigations at this level may include model access management, physical security controls, authentication measures, endpoint security, access management, secure model storage, vulnerability detection & management, detection of & response to suspected malicious activity.
paraphrase: Footnote 11 lists example mitigations at this security level, including access management, physical security, authentication, endpoint security, secure storage, and vulnerability/threat detection.

section_heading: Table 2.2.3.a: Harmful Manipulation CCLs and Security Mitigations
excerpt: 1 (exploratory): Possesses manipulative capabilities sufficient to enable it to systematically and substantially change beliefs and behavior in identified high stakes contexts over the course of interactions with the model, reasonably resulting in additional expected harm at severe scale.
paraphrase: This CCL is defined as the model having manipulative capabilities capable of systematically and substantially changing beliefs and behavior in high-stakes contexts, resulting in severe-scale harm.

section_heading: Table 2.2.3.a: Harmful Manipulation CCLs and Security Mitigations
locator: Table 2.2.3.a / 1 (exploratory) / Recommended security level and rationale
context_stem: Row: 1 (exploratory); Column: Recommended security level and rationale
excerpt: The lower velocity of harm scenarios associated with this CCL and the viability of social defenses against large scale misuse of such models count against security mitigations with substantial costs to innovation.
paraphrase: The rationale explains that slower harm velocity and viable social defenses argue against costly security mitigations for this CCL.

excerpt: This section describes our mitigation approach for models that pose risks of severe harm through machine learning R&D, and then details our set of ML R&D CCLs, as well as the mitigations that we provisionally assess as appropriate for them.
paraphrase: The section introduces the mitigation approach and ML R&D CCLs along with provisionally assessed mitigations.

excerpt: As with misuse CCLs, we designate security and deployment mitigations for ML R&D CCLs, although deployment mitigations focus on different threat models and therefore also include measures for large scale internal deployments.
paraphrase: Security and deployment mitigations are designated for ML R&D CCLs, with deployment mitigations addressing different threat models including large scale internal deployments.

excerpt: Security mitigations against exfiltration risk are important for models reaching ML R&D CCLs, because the exfiltration of highly capable models increases the likelihood they will be misused to achieve other critical capabilities, or deployed without adequate control and oversight.
paraphrase: Security mitigations against exfiltration matter for ML R&D CCL models because exfiltration raises the risk of misuse or uncontrolled deployment.

excerpt: Below, we rely again on security levels to articulate the security goal recommended for each CCL. Security mitigations also protect against the risk of the model exfiltrating itself.
paraphrase: Security levels are again used to articulate recommended security goals per CCL, and these mitigations also guard against a model exfiltrating itself.

excerpt: The following mitigation process will be applied for deployments of a model reaching a ML R&D CCL. The approach is similar to misuse deployment mitigations, with an added focus on large scale internal deployments.
paraphrase: A described mitigation process applies to deployments of models reaching an ML R&D CCL, similar to misuse deployment mitigations but with added focus on large-scale internal deployments.

excerpt: Development and assessment of mitigations: safeguards and an accompanying safety case are developed by iterating on the following:
paraphrase: The first stage involves iteratively developing safeguards and a supporting safety case.

context_stem: Development and assessment of mitigations: safeguards and an accompanying safety case are developed by iterating on the following:
excerpt: Developing and improving a suite of safeguards targeting the capability, which may include measures such as limiting affordances, monitoring and escalation, auditing, and alignment training, in addition to measures for preventing large scale misuse.
paraphrase: One step is developing and refining safeguards targeting the capability, such as limiting affordances, monitoring/escalation, auditing, alignment training, and misuse prevention measures.

context_stem: Development and assessment of mitigations: safeguards and an accompanying safety case are developed by iterating on the following:
excerpt: Assessing the robustness of these mitigations against the risk posed in both internal and external deployment through testing (e.g. automated evaluations, red teaming) and threat modeling research. The assessment takes the form of a safety case, taking into account factors such as:
paraphrase: Another step is assessing mitigation robustness against internal and external deployment risks through testing and threat modeling, forming a safety case that considers several factors.

context_stem: Assessing the robustness of these mitigations... takes into account factors such as:
excerpt: How much the risk has been reduced by mitigations. For example, tests run on the safeguards may suggest that it is very unlikely they can be circumvented by external threat actors or the model in question to increase ML R&D risk.
paraphrase: One factor is the degree of risk reduction achieved by mitigations, illustrated by test results suggesting low likelihood of circumvention.

context_stem: Assessing the robustness of these mitigations... takes into account factors such as:
excerpt: The likelihood and consequences of model misuse or misalignment, capability improvements after the risk assessment, and likelihood and consequences of our mitigations being circumvented, deactivated, or subverted.
paraphrase: Another factor is the likelihood and consequences of misuse, misalignment, post-assessment capability gains, and mitigation circumvention.

context_stem: Assessing the robustness of these mitigations... takes into account factors such as:
excerpt: The scope of the deployment. For example, small scale and private deployments may pose substantially less risk than large scale or public deployments.
paraphrase: Another factor is deployment scope, since small/private deployments may pose less risk than large-scale/public ones.

context_stem: Assessing the robustness of these mitigations... takes into account factors such as:
excerpt: Model propensity for, historical incidence of and severity of related events: for example, such data may suggest a high (or low) likelihood of misalignment in or misuse of models at the CCL, and mitigations would consequently have to be stronger (or not as strong) for deployment to be appropriate.
paraphrase: Another factor is historical data on model propensity and event severity, which may indicate whether stronger or weaker mitigations are needed at that CCL.

excerpt: Pre-deployment review of safety case: external deployments and large scale internal deployments of a model take place only after the appropriate governance function determines the safety case regarding each CCL the model has reached to be adequate.
paraphrase: External and large-scale internal deployments only proceed after governance approval of the safety case for each reached CCL.

excerpt: In particular, we will deem deployment mitigations adequate if the evidence suggests that for the CCLs the model has reached, the increase in likelihood of severe harm has been reduced to an acceptable level.
paraphrase: Mitigations are considered adequate when evidence shows the increased likelihood of severe harm has been reduced to an acceptable level.

excerpt: Post-deployment processes: our safety cases and mitigations may be updated if deemed necessary by post-market monitoring. Material updates to a safety case will be submitted to the appropriate governance function for review.
paraphrase: Post-deployment, safety cases and mitigations may be updated based on monitoring, and material updates require governance review.

excerpt: This process is designed to ensure that residual risk remains at acceptable levels: evidence of efficacy collected during development and testing, as well as expert-driven estimates of other parameters, will enable us to assess residual risk and to detect substantial changes that invalidate our risk assessment.
paraphrase: The process aims to keep residual risk acceptable by using efficacy evidence and expert estimates to assess risk and detect invalidating changes.

excerpt: With iteration on safeguards and safety cases, we believe that we are able to make informed decisions about the level of risk via a CCL before a model is released or deployed internally at scale, and reliably prevent models posing unacceptable levels of risk from being deployed.
paraphrase: Iterating on safeguards and safety cases is believed to enable informed risk decisions before release and reliably block unacceptably risky models from deployment.

excerpt: The table below details a set of ML R&D CCLs we have identified that may lead to heightened severe risk through ML R&D. We expect these to evolve over time.
paraphrase: The table lists identified ML R&D CCLs that could lead to heightened severe risk, expected to evolve over time.

excerpt: We recommend a security level for each of these CCLs, which reflect our assessment of the minimum appropriate level of security the field of frontier AI should apply to models reaching each CCL.
paraphrase: A security level is recommended for each CCL, reflecting the assessed minimum appropriate security the frontier AI field should apply.

excerpt: These CCLs focus on risks posed by models capable of accelerating the rate of AI progress.
paraphrase: This subsection's CCLs address risks from models that can accelerate AI progress.

excerpt: These capabilities may indicate a heightened ability to undermine human control of models, may incentivize greater (and therefore higher risk) deployment of models, and could also result in the unsafe attainment or proliferation of other powerful AI models if misused by external threat actors.
paraphrase: Such capabilities may signal increased ability to undermine human control, incentivize riskier deployment, and enable unsafe proliferation of powerful models if misused.

section_heading: Table 3.2.1.a: Machine Learning R&D CCLs and Security Mitigations
locator: Table 3.2.1.a / ML R&D acceleration level 1 / Critical Capability Level
context_stem: Row: ML R&D acceleration level 1; Column: Critical Capability Level
excerpt: ML R&D acceleration level 1: Has been used to accelerate AI development, resulting in AI progress substantially accelerating from historical rates.
paraphrase: This CCL is defined as the model having been used to accelerate AI development such that progress substantially exceeds historical rates.

excerpt: Security level 3
paraphrase: The recommended security level for ML R&D acceleration level 1 is Security level 3.

section_heading: Table 3.2.1.a: Machine Learning R&D CCLs and Security Mitigations
locator: Table 3.2.1.a / ML R&D acceleration level 1 / Recommended security level and rationale (rationale text)
context_stem: Row: ML R&D acceleration level 1; Column: Recommended security level and rationale
excerpt: Unrestricted access to models at this level of capability could significantly increase a threat actor's ability to progress to yet more powerful models and other critical capabilities. The exfiltration of such a model may therefore have a significant effect on society's ability to adapt to and govern powerful AI models, effects that may have long-lasting consequences.
paraphrase: Unrestricted access at this capability level could help threat actors reach more powerful models, and exfiltration could have long-lasting effects on society's governance of powerful AI.

section_heading: Table 3.2.1.a: Machine Learning R&D CCLs and Security Mitigations
locator: Table 3.2.1.a / ML R&D acceleration level 1 / Recommended security level and rationale (rationale text 2)
context_stem: Row: ML R&D acceleration level 1; Column: Recommended security level and rationale
excerpt: Substantially strengthened security is therefore recommended.
paraphrase: The rationale concludes that substantially strengthened security is recommended.

section_heading: Table 3.2.1.a: Machine Learning R&D CCLs and Security Mitigations
locator: Table 3.2.1.a / ML R&D acceleration level 1 / Recommended security level and rationale (caveat)
context_stem: Row: ML R&D acceleration level 1; Column: Recommended security level and rationale
excerpt: However, we expect that acceleration will stem from systems of models integrated with workflows, rather than the model alone. The overall reduced impact of model weights counts against security levels with substantial innovation costs.
paraphrase: The rationale notes acceleration likely comes from integrated systems rather than the model alone, which argues against high-cost security levels.

excerpt: The same caveats regarding security levels for misuse CCLs apply.
paraphrase: Footnote 14 notes that the same caveats for misuse CCL security levels also apply here.

excerpt: This level may include mitigations aligned with SL 2, plus additional mitigations designed to prevent unilateral access, harden infrastructure, and prevent data exfiltration.
paraphrase: Footnote 15 explains this security level may include SL 2 mitigations plus additional measures against unilateral access, infrastructure hardening, and data exfiltration prevention.

section_heading: Table 3.2.1.a: Machine Learning R&D CCLs and Security Mitigations
locator: Table 3.2.1.a / ML R&D automation level 1 / Critical Capability Level
context_stem: Row: ML R&D automation level 1; Column: Critical Capability Level
excerpt: ML R&D automation level 1: Can fully automate the work of any team of researchers at Google focused on improving AI capabilities, with approximately comparable all-inclusive costs.
paraphrase: This CCL is defined as the model being able to fully automate any Google AI capabilities research team's work at comparable cost.

section_heading: Table 3.2.1.a: Machine Learning R&D CCLs and Security Mitigations
locator: Table 3.2.1.a / ML R&D automation level 1 / Recommended security level and rationale
context_stem: Row: ML R&D automation level 1; Column: Recommended security level and rationale
excerpt: We recommend Security level 4 for this capability threshold, but emphasize that this must be taken on by the frontier AI field as a whole.
paraphrase: Security level 4 is recommended for this threshold, with emphasis that the whole frontier AI field must adopt it.

section_heading: Table 3.2.1.a: Machine Learning R&D CCLs and Security Mitigations
locator: Table 3.2.1.a / ML R&D automation level 1 / Recommended security level and rationale (rationale)
context_stem: Row: ML R&D automation level 1; Column: Recommended security level and rationale
excerpt: Unrestricted access to models at this level of capability could give an actor (or AI systems) with adequate computational resources the ability to reach capabilities much more powerful than those in the other CCLs listed in a short amount of time.
paraphrase: Unrestricted access at this level could let an actor with sufficient compute quickly reach far more powerful capabilities than other listed CCLs.

section_heading: Table 3.2.1.a: Machine Learning R&D CCLs and Security Mitigations
locator: Table 3.2.1.a / ML R&D automation level 1 / Recommended security level and rationale (rationale 2)
context_stem: Row: ML R&D automation level 1; Column: Recommended security level and rationale
excerpt: This could be catastrophic if there is no effective way of defending against rapidly improving and potentially superhuman AI systems wielded by threat actors.
paraphrase: Without effective defenses against rapidly improving, possibly superhuman AI wielded by threat actors, this could be catastrophic.

section_heading: Table 3.2.1.a: Machine Learning R&D CCLs and Security Mitigations
locator: Table 3.2.1.a / ML R&D automation level 1 / Recommended security level and rationale (conclusion)
context_stem: Row: ML R&D automation level 1; Column: Recommended security level and rationale
excerpt: Therefore, we recommend models at this level of capability have exceptional security even though they may have substantial innovation costs.
paraphrase: Exceptional security is recommended for this capability level despite potentially substantial innovation costs.

excerpt: This level may include mitigations aligned with SL 2 and 3, plus additional mitigations aimed to isolate model weights, enhanced data center security, further hardening of infrastructure and minimizing potential attack surface.
paraphrase: Footnote 16 explains this level may include SL 2 and 3 mitigations plus measures to isolate model weights, enhance data center security, harden infrastructure, and minimize attack surface.

excerpt: Misalignment can pose a number of risks. In the context of the Framework, we address specific scenarios where general-purpose AI agents are potentially misaligned and can become difficult to control, thereby posing a risk of severe harm.
paraphrase: Misalignment poses several risks; the Framework addresses scenarios where misaligned general-purpose AI agents become difficult to control, risking severe harm.

excerpt: Here we describe an approach for addressing misalignment risk that focuses specifically on when models may develop a baseline instrumental reasoning ability at which, without additional mitigations, they may have the potential to undermine human control.
paraphrase: The approach focuses on the point at which models develop baseline instrumental reasoning ability that could, absent mitigations, undermine human control.

excerpt: When models reach this capability level, one possible mitigation is to apply an automated monitor to the model's explicit reasoning (e.g. chain-of-thought output).
paraphrase: One possible mitigation upon reaching this capability level is applying an automated monitor to the model's explicit reasoning output.

excerpt: Once a model is capable of effective instrumental reasoning in ways that cannot be monitored, additional mitigations may be warranted—the development of which is an area of active research.
paraphrase: Once instrumental reasoning becomes unmonitorable, further mitigations may be needed, and developing them is an active research area.

excerpt: Given its nascency, we expect our approach to misalignment risk to evolve substantially. This section is therefore illustrative only.
paraphrase: Because the approach is nascent, it is expected to evolve substantially, and this section is illustrative only.

excerpt: Accordingly, we do not indicate security mitigations for models at these CCLs. The table below summarizes the initial approach:
paraphrase: No security mitigations are indicated for models at these CCLs, and the table summarizes the initial approach.

section_heading: Table 4.a: Exploratory Misalignment CCLs and Mitigations
locator: Table 4.a / Instrumental Reasoning Level 1 / Illustrative Instrumental Reasoning CCL
context_stem: Row: Instrumental Reasoning Level 1; Column: Illustrative Instrumental Reasoning CCL
excerpt: Instrumental Reasoning Level 1: The instrumental reasoning abilities of the model enable enough situational awareness (ability to work out and use relevant details of its deployment setting) and stealth (ability to circumvent basic oversight mechanisms) such that, absent additional mitigations, we cannot rule out the model significantly undermining human control.
paraphrase: This CCL is defined as the model having enough situational awareness and stealth via instrumental reasoning that, without mitigations, it could undermine human control.

section_heading: Table 4.a: Exploratory Misalignment CCLs and Mitigations
locator: Table 4.a / Instrumental Reasoning Level 1 / Illustrative Mitigation
context_stem: Row: Instrumental Reasoning Level 1; Column: Illustrative Mitigation
excerpt: Automated monitoring: monitoring system to detect illicit use of instrumental reasoning capabilities in a model's chain-of-thought may be applied in high-stakes internal deployments where there is significant risk of the model undermining human control.
paraphrase: The illustrative mitigation is an automated monitoring system for detecting illicit instrumental reasoning use in chain-of-thought, applied in high-stakes internal deployments with significant risk.

section_heading: Table 4.a: Exploratory Misalignment CCLs and Mitigations
locator: Table 4.a / Instrumental Reasoning Level 2 / Illustrative Instrumental Reasoning CCL
context_stem: Row: Instrumental Reasoning Level 2; Column: Illustrative Instrumental Reasoning CCL
excerpt: Instrumental Reasoning Level 2: The instrumental reasoning abilities of the model enable enough situational awareness and stealth that, even when relevant model outputs (including, e.g. scratchpads) are being monitored, we cannot detect or rule out the risk of a model significantly undermining human control.
paraphrase: This CCL is defined as the model having enough situational awareness and stealth that even monitored outputs cannot rule out undermining human control.

section_heading: Table 4.a: Exploratory Misalignment CCLs and Mitigations
locator: Table 4.a / Instrumental Reasoning Level 2 / Illustrative Mitigation
context_stem: Row: Instrumental Reasoning Level 2; Column: Illustrative Mitigation
excerpt: Future work: We are actively researching approaches to addressing models that reach this CCL.
paraphrase: Mitigation for this CCL is still under active research, with no defined approach yet.

excerpt: The Frontier Safety Framework will be updated at least once a year—more frequently if we have reasonable grounds to believe the adequacy of the Framework or our adherence to it has been materially undermined.
paraphrase: The Framework will be updated at least annually, or more often if there is reason to believe its adequacy or adherence has been materially undermined.

excerpt: The process will involve (i) an assessment of the Framework's appropriateness for the management of systemic risk, drawing on information sources such as record of adherence to the framework, relevant high-quality research, information shared through industry forums, and evaluation results, as necessary, and (ii) an assessment of our adherence to the Framework.
paraphrase: The update process includes assessing the Framework's appropriateness using various information sources, and assessing GDM's own adherence to it.

excerpt: Following this assessment, we may:
paraphrase: The following list describes possible actions following the assessment.

excerpt: Update our risk domains and CCLs, where necessary.
paraphrase: Risk domains and CCLs may be updated as necessary.

excerpt: Update our testing and mitigation approaches, where needed to ensure risk remains adequately assessed and addressed according to our current understanding.
paraphrase: Testing and mitigation approaches may be updated as needed to ensure risk continues to be adequately assessed and addressed.

excerpt: The updated version and framework assessment will be reviewed by the appropriate corporate governance bodies.
paraphrase: Corporate governance bodies will review the updated version and framework assessment.

excerpt: If we assess that a model has reached a CCL that poses an unmitigated and material risk to overall public safety, we aim to share relevant information with appropriate government authorities where it will facilitate safety of frontier AI.
paraphrase: If a model reaches a CCL posing unmitigated material risk to public safety, GDM aims to share relevant information with government authorities where it aids frontier AI safety.

excerpt: Where appropriate, and subject to adequate confidentiality and security measures and considerations around proprietary and sensitive information, this information may include:
paraphrase: Subject to confidentiality, security, and sensitivity considerations, the shared information may include the following categories.

excerpt: Model information: characteristics of the AI model relevant to the risk it may pose with its critical capabilities.
paraphrase: One category of shareable information is model characteristics relevant to its critical-capability risk.

excerpt: Evaluation results: such as details about the evaluation design, the results, and any robustness tests.
paraphrase: Another category is evaluation results, including design details, results, and robustness tests.

excerpt: Mitigation plans: descriptions of our mitigation plans and how they are expected to reduce the risk.
paraphrase: The third category is mitigation plan descriptions and their expected risk-reduction effects.

excerpt: We may also consider disclosing information to other external organisations to promote shared learning and coordinated risk mitigation.
paraphrase: GDM may also consider disclosing information to other external organisations to support shared learning and coordinated risk mitigation.

excerpt: We will continue to review and evolve our disclosure process over time.
paraphrase: The disclosure process will continue to be reviewed and evolved over time.
